stem: Which of the following does not contain any coordinate bond?
solution:
$\text{HF}_2^-$ is the only species among the given options which does not contain any coordinate bond because it is held by hydrogen bonding.

stem: In a 1st order reaction, reactant concentration $C$ varies with time $t$ as:
solution: For a first order reaction, $\log C = \log C_0 - \dfrac{kt}{2.303}$, so a plot of $\log C$ vs $t$ is a straight line with slope $= -\dfrac{k}{2.303}$.

stem: Which of the following represents the correct order of Cl–O bond lengths in $\text{ClO}^-, \text{ClO}_2^-, \text{ClO}_3^-, \text{ClO}_4^-$?
solution:
The b.o. in $\text{Cl}-\text{O}^-$ is 1

The b.o. in $\text{O}=\text{Cl}-\text{O}^-$ is 1.5

The b.o. in $\text{ClO}_3^-$ is $\dfrac{5}{3} = 1.66$

The b.o. in $\text{ClO}_4^-$ is $\dfrac{7}{4} = 1.75$

The bond length increases as b.o. decreases.

stem: Which one of the following ions has the maximum magnetic moment?
solution: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($d^5$) has 5 unpaired electrons, therefore magnetic moment $= \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = 5.91$ BM, which is maximum among given options, as $\text{Sc}^{3+}, \text{Ti}^{3+}, \text{Cr}^{3+}$ contain 0, 1 and 3 unpaired electrons respectively.

stem: The difference in the number of unpaired electrons of a metal ion in its high-spin and low-spin octahedral complexes is two. The metal ion is
solution:
$\text{Co}^{2+}$ ($d^7$): high spin $t_{2g}^5e_g^2$ has 3 unpaired electrons; low spin $t_{2g}^6e_g^1$ has 1 unpaired electron. Difference $= 2$.

(For $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, $d^6$: 4 vs 0; $\text{Mn}^{2+}$, $d^5$: 5 vs 1; $\text{Ni}^{2+}$, $d^8$: 2 vs 2.)
